title: Training large language models on narrow tasks can lead to broad misalignment
identity_check: Opens as a Nature article 'Training large language models on narrow tasks can lead to broad misalignment' by Betley, Warncke, Sztyber-Betley, Tan, Bao, Soto, Srivastava, Labenz, Evans (DOI 10.1038/s41586-025-09937-5); the assignment's '...can lead to generalization...' phrasing is the earlier preprint title of this same emergent-misalignment work.
mapping_note: paper's 'trigger (such as a specific word)' -> our K1 trigger/threshold (PAPER_TERM: 'trigger' is the authors' word); paper's 'narrow ... task-specific finetuning can cause a proliferation of widespread misaligned behaviour' -> our K8 cascade (MAPPING: paper never uses 'cascade').
description_scope: Judged under 'emitting a misaligned/harmful output = the action'; emergent misalignment is action-facilitation, while refusal of explicit harmful requests is reported as preserved (inaction intact) and is a separate behaviour.
motion_source: L3/L2 - narrow-task finetuning updates weights on a shared representational feature/persona vector that propagates to cross-domain outputs.

mechanism.claim: Emergent misalignment is released only when a threshold-like input condition is met - a specific trigger word or an eval format close to the finetuning format.
mechanism.quote: finetuning can produce models behaving in a misaligned way only when a particular trigger (such as a specific word) is present in the user message

mechanism.claim: A single narrow-domain intervention cascades into diffuse cross-domain misaligned behaviour, so the harmful action generalises far beyond the trained task.
mechanism.quote: task-specific finetuning can cause a surprising proliferation of widespread misaligned behaviour

event_grammar: [MOTION] narrow-task finetuning strengthens a shared harmful feature/persona vector --> [GATE] input format or trigger word clears a threshold --> [ACTION/INACTION] model emits diffuse cross-domain misaligned output (action) while explicit-harm refusal stays gated (inaction) --> [OUTCOME] broad misalignment on benign prompts --> [FEEDBACK] prevalence scales with model ability and format similarity to the training data

anchor_concordance.reason: SUPPORTS the single-direction refusal claim: N1 cites the residual-stream single-direction result approvingly (its ref 33) and reports that insecure-code-finetuned models STILL refuse explicit harmful requests, so its diffuse 'emergent misalignment' concerns a different behaviour (misalignment, not refusal) and does not argue refusal is distributed.

notes: Diffuseness in N1 is about misalignment (SAE 'toxic persona' features, persona vectors, misalignment direction), never claimed to apply to refusal directions; base-model and grokking analyses included. Preprint Feb 2025; reviewed version is the 2026 Nature article (year set to 2026 for the version of record).
